# ECN-2026-025 Change notice - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Reason for change
- Background: Recent maintenance audits and lubricant analysis samples identified accelerated wear signatures on the main roll bearings of the Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01). Trending in vibration and oil particle counts, reviewed against the existing maintenance practice, indicates that lubrication frequency is a principal contributor to the observed condition. Laboratory commentary recommended shortening the time between replenishment to reduce contamination loading and restore hydrodynamic film integrity.
- Objective: Standardize the main roll bearing lubrication to a defined interval to reduce wear rates, extend component life, and reduce unplanned downtime risk. This change aligns maintenance practice with the findings in related engineering notices and standard operating procedures to ensure consistent application across the line and supporting documentation.
- Rationale: Implementing a documented, shorter lubrication interval provides a simple, auditable action that directly addresses the root-cause indicators from oil analysis and bearing inspections. The interval decision was selected to balance operational availability with lubricant contamination control, minimize bearing metal-to-metal contact risk, and provide a repeatable baseline for future trend analysis and corrective actions.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01).  
- Components affected: Main roll bearings and associated lubrication system components (feed lines, reservoirs, strainers, and gauge points used for sampling).  
- Documentation affected: Maintenance task lists and log templates for EQ-P1-L1-RR01; operator shift handover checklists that include bearing condition notes; lubrication consumption and inventory records; oil analysis sampling schedule records used for trend tracking. See related documents ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for prior condition assessments and supporting analysis, and SOP-P1-L1-02 for operating interface and handover requirements.

Implementation
- New requirement: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. This interval supersedes prior informal practice and becomes the controlled interval to be recorded in maintenance execution and equipment history records.
- Tasks and responsibilities:
  - Maintenance planners: Update the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) task for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 to reflect the new interval. Ensure work order templates include fields for lubricant type, quantity added, sight/level confirmation, and initial oil cleanliness check result.
  - Maintenance technicians: Perform lubrication per the updated work order. Record lubricant batch identifier, amount added, and any abnormal findings. Attach an oil sample label when contamination is suspected and route sample to the laboratory per existing sampling protocol in SOP-P1-L1-02.
  - Operators: Perform pre-lubrication checks at shift handover and log any visible leaks, unusual noise, or temperature anomalies to the maintenance queue as required by SOP-P1-L1-02.
  - Reliability engineers: Monitor trend data after implementation, comparing vibration and oil analysis results against pre-change baseline from ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040. Provide a summary of trend performance at the next scheduled review.
- Procedure details and examples:
  - Use approved lubricant specified in the current equipment lubrication matrix; confirm compatibility with reservoir and seals before addition. If label or batch is unclear, escalate to the reliability engineer.
  - Example record entries: work order reference, technician initials, main roll bearing lubrication interval confirmation (entered as 120 hours), lubricant batch ID, liters added, and oil sample taken Y/N. Maintain a physical copy of the work order on the equipment maintenance binder for shift access and attach the electronic record in the CMMS.
  - Sampling: When oil appears discolored or particle counts exceed guideline threshold, collect a routed sample and reference ECN-2026-034 for prior sample context. Mark sample with equipment id EQ-P1-L1-RR01 and work order reference.
- Training and communication:
  - Conduct a focused briefing with maintenance and operations covering the new interval, recording expectations, and escalation paths. Use SOP-P1-L1-02 as the operator interface reference for shift responsibilities.
  - Post visible change notices at the equipment and in the maintenance office summarizing the new lubrication requirement and referencing this document and related documents ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for background.

Records to keep
- Maintain work order copies and CMMS entries showing lubrication performed at the new interval for EQ-P1-L1-RR01. Records should include lubricant batch IDs and any abnormal findings.
- Preserve oil analysis results and trend charts used to justify the interval, referencing the prior notices ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for continuity.
- Training attendance logs and signed acknowledgements from personnel briefed on the change, retained according to document control practice.

Approvals
- Approval chain must include maintenance manager, reliability engineer, operations supervisor, and document control. Approvers shall reference this ECN id in approval records and ensure CMMS entries are updated after approval.
- Post-implementation review: Reliability engineering to perform a review of lubricant consumption and condition trends after a sustained period of lubrication at the specified interval and provide recommendations for further adjustment if necessary. Refer to ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for comparative analysis and SOP-P1-L1-02 for operator interaction during review cycles.
